paragraphs.title: The Lord’s Appointed Feasts and the Sabbath

easy.question: Who spoke to Moses at the beginning of the passage?
answers: The Lord
Pharaoh
Aaron
easy.explanation: The first verse says, “The Lord spoke to Moses.”

easy.question: How many days shall work be done before the Sabbath?
answers: Seven days
Six days
Five days
easy.explanation: The passage says, “Six days shall work be done.”

easy.question: What is the seventh day called?
answers: A workday
Passover
A Sabbath of rest
easy.explanation: The seventh day is called “the sabbath of rest.”

medium.question: What order of the week is described in the passage?
answers: Six days of work followed by a day of rest
A day of rest followed by six days of work
Every day is a day of rest
medium.explanation: The passage first mentions six days of work and then the seventh-day Sabbath.

medium.question: What does “holy convocations” mean in this context?
answers: Special kinds of work
Sacred gatherings or holy occasions
Places to live
medium.explanation: The phrase describes appointed times for sacred assembly or observance.

medium.question: What does “all your dwellings” mean in “the sabbath of the Lord in all your dwellings”?
answers: Your feasts
Your work
The places where you live
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to every place where the Israelites live.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from “the feasts of the Lord” and “which ye shall proclaim to be holy convocations”?
answers: The Lord appoints the times, and Israel observes them as holy
Israel chooses all the times independently
The times are intended only for Moses
challenge.explanation: They are called the Lord’s feasts, while Israel is commanded to proclaim them holy.

challenge.question: What does “in their seasons” mean in verse 4?
answers: Only during wartime
At the appointed time for each feast
Every day according to personal choice
challenge.explanation: Each feast has a set time when it is to be observed.

challenge.question: What may be surprising about the list of appointed times?
answers: Only harvest festivals are mentioned
Moses is the first feast listed
The weekly Sabbath is included among the Lord’s feasts
challenge.explanation: Although it occurs every week, the Sabbath is listed first among these holy appointed times.

questions.question: What can be inferred from “the feasts of the Lord” and “which ye shall proclaim to be holy convocations”?
answers: The Lord appoints the times, and Israel observes them as holy
Israel chooses all the times independently
The times are intended only for Moses
questions.explanation: They are called the Lord’s feasts, while Israel is commanded to proclaim them holy.

questions.question: What does “in their seasons” mean in verse 4?
answers: Only during wartime
At the appointed time for each feast
Every day according to personal choice
questions.explanation: Each feast has a set time when it is to be observed.

questions.question: What may be surprising about the list of appointed times?
answers: Only harvest festivals are mentioned
Moses is the first feast listed
The weekly Sabbath is included among the Lord’s feasts
questions.explanation: Although it occurs every week, the Sabbath is listed first among these holy appointed times.

paragraphs.title: Passover and the Feast of Unleavened Bread

easy.question: On what day of the first month does Passover occur?
answers: The fourteenth day
The fifteenth day
The seventh day
easy.explanation: Passover is on the fourteenth day of the first month.

easy.question: How long does the Feast of Unleavened Bread last?
answers: Three days
Seven days
Fourteen days
easy.explanation: The passage says, “Seven days ye must eat unleavened bread.”

easy.question: What is forbidden on the first and seventh days of the feast?
answers: Eating unleavened bread
Offering a sacrifice
Doing servile work
easy.explanation: No servile work is to be done on either day.

medium.question: What is the correct order of events?
answers: Passover on the fourteenth, the feast begins on the fifteenth, then seven feast days
The feast begins on the fourteenth, Passover is on the fifteenth, then one day
Seven feast days begin on the fourteenth, followed by Passover on the fifteenth
medium.explanation: Passover comes on the fourteenth, followed by the seven-day feast beginning on the fifteenth.

medium.question: In “the first day ye shall have an holy convocation,” what does “holy convocation” mean?
answers: A day of Torah reading only
A special day of sacred assembly
A day when work is required
medium.explanation: The context presents it as a holy day on which servile work is forbidden.

medium.question: Why are both the first and seventh days emphasized?
answers: Because servile work is forbidden on both
Because unleavened bread is eaten only on those days
Because they always fall on the same date
medium.explanation: Both days are holy convocations on which servile work may not be done.

challenge.question: What distinguishes Passover from the beginning of the Feast of Unleavened Bread?
answers: Passover is on the fourteenth, and the feast begins on the fifteenth
Passover lasts seven days, and the feast lasts one day
Passover is on the seventh day, and the feast begins on the fourteenth
challenge.explanation: Passover is observed on the fourteenth day, while the feast begins on the fifteenth.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from forbidding servile work on both the first and seventh days?
answers: Only the middle of the feast is holy
The holiness of the feast is emphasized at its beginning and end
The feast lasts only two days
challenge.explanation: The two endpoints of the seven-day period receive special emphasis.

challenge.question: What is observed throughout all seven days, not only on the first or last?
answers: Eating unleavened bread and offering sacrifices
Only abstaining from work
A holy convocation every day
challenge.explanation: Unleavened bread is eaten for seven days, and offerings are made throughout the period; the holy convocations and work restrictions especially concern the first and seventh days.

questions.question: What distinguishes Passover from the beginning of the Feast of Unleavened Bread?
answers: Passover is on the fourteenth, and the feast begins on the fifteenth
Passover lasts seven days, and the feast lasts one day
Passover is on the seventh day, and the feast begins on the fourteenth
questions.explanation: Passover is observed on the fourteenth day, while the feast begins on the fifteenth.

questions.question: What can be inferred from forbidding servile work on both the first and seventh days?
answers: Only the middle of the feast is holy
The holiness of the feast is emphasized at its beginning and end
The feast lasts only two days
questions.explanation: The two endpoints of the seven-day period receive special emphasis.

questions.question: What is observed throughout all seven days, not only on the first or last?
answers: Eating unleavened bread and offering sacrifices
Only abstaining from work
A holy convocation every day
questions.explanation: Unleavened bread is eaten for seven days, and offerings are made throughout the period; the holy convocations and work restrictions especially concern the first and seventh days.

paragraphs.title: The Sheaf and the Firstfruits of the Harvest

easy.question: To whom is the sheaf of the firstfruits brought?
answers: The priest
The king
The city elders
easy.explanation: The sheaf is brought to the priest.

easy.question: What animal is offered on the day the sheaf is waved?
answers: A one-year-old goat
A one-year-old lamb without blemish
A two-year-old bull
easy.explanation: A male lamb of the first year is offered as a burnt offering.

easy.question: What may not be eaten until the offering is brought?
answers: Only fruit
Only meat
Bread, parched grain, or fresh ears
easy.explanation: The passage forbids bread, parched grain, and fresh ears until that day.

medium.question: What is the correct order of events?
answers: Harvesting, bringing the sheaf to the priest, and waving it
Waving the sheaf, harvesting, and bringing it to the priest
Eating the grain, harvesting, and offering the lamb
medium.explanation: The harvest is gathered, the sheaf is brought to the priest, and the priest waves it before the Lord.

medium.question: In “he shall wave the sheaf before the Lord,” what does “wave” mean?
answers: Hide
Lift or move before the Lord
Eat
medium.explanation: The priest presents the sheaf before the Lord by lifting or waving it.

medium.question: Why may the new grain not be eaten until the offering is brought?
answers: To wait for rain
So the priest can choose the grain
Because the offering must come before eating it
medium.explanation: The passage expressly connects the restriction with bringing the offering.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from calling the sheaf “the firstfruits of your harvest”?
answers: It represents the beginning of the grain harvest offered to the Lord
It is the final harvest of the year
It is intended only for the priest to eat
challenge.explanation: Firstfruits are the first portion of the harvest, offered before the rest is used.

challenge.question: Which phrase shows that this command applies beyond one generation?
answers: “For a sweet savour”
“A statute for ever throughout your generations”
“Of the first year”
challenge.explanation: This phrase explicitly extends the statute through future generations.

challenge.question: What is the relationship between waving the sheaf and eating the new grain?
answers: It may be eaten first if it is cooked
The sheaf is waved only after everyone has eaten
The sheaf and offering come before eating the new grain
challenge.explanation: The grain may not be eaten until the offering has been brought.

questions.question: What can be inferred from calling the sheaf “the firstfruits of your harvest”?
answers: It represents the beginning of the grain harvest offered to the Lord
It is the final harvest of the year
It is intended only for the priest to eat
questions.explanation: Firstfruits are the first portion of the harvest, offered before the rest is used.

questions.question: Which phrase shows that this command applies beyond one generation?
answers: “For a sweet savour”
“A statute for ever throughout your generations”
“Of the first year”
questions.explanation: This phrase explicitly extends the statute through future generations.

questions.question: What is the relationship between waving the sheaf and eating the new grain?
answers: It may be eaten first if it is cooked
The sheaf is waved only after everyone has eaten
The sheaf and offering come before eating the new grain
questions.explanation: The grain may not be eaten until the offering has been brought.

paragraphs.title: Counting the Weeks and the Two Loaves

easy.question: How many days are counted before the new offering is brought?
answers: Fifty days
Seven days
Thirty days
easy.explanation: The passage says, “Even unto the morrow after the seventh sabbath shall ye number fifty days.”

easy.question: How many loaves are brought as a wave offering?
answers: One loaf
Two loaves
Seven loaves
easy.explanation: Two wave loaves are brought.

easy.question: What is forbidden on the holy convocation?
answers: Eating bread
Counting the days
Doing servile work
easy.explanation: No servile work is to be done on that day.

medium.question: What order of events is described?
answers: Count the days, bring a new offering, and observe a holy convocation
Offer a goat, count the days, and then bring bread
Observe a day of rest, begin counting, and then bring the sheaf
medium.explanation: The people count seven weeks and fifty days, bring a new offering, and observe a holy convocation.

medium.question: In “bring out of your habitations two wave loaves,” what does “habitations” mean?
answers: The sanctuary only
The places where you live
The wilderness
medium.explanation: The loaves are brought from the people’s homes or settlements.

medium.question: Which description of the sacrifices matches the passage?
answers: Two goats for a sin offering and seven lambs for peace offerings
One bull for a sin offering and two lambs for a burnt offering
One male goat for a sin offering and two lambs for peace offerings
medium.explanation: The passage specifies one kid of the goats for a sin offering and two lambs for peace offerings.

challenge.question: What does the combination of “holy convocation” and “no servile work” show?
answers: It is a special day of sacred assembly and abstaining from work
It is an ordinary workday
It is a day devoted only to counting
challenge.explanation: The verse joins sacred assembly with a prohibition against servile work.

challenge.question: Why are the loaves called “firstfruits”?
answers: They are eaten first at every meal
They are the first produce dedicated to the Lord
They are baked only at the beginning of the year
challenge.explanation: “Firstfruits” means the first produce brought and dedicated to the Lord.

challenge.question: How many animals are mentioned in all the offerings in verses 18–19?
answers: Ten
Eleven
Thirteen
challenge.explanation: There are seven lambs, one bull, two rams, one goat, and two lambs—thirteen animals in all.

questions.question: What does the combination of “holy convocation” and “no servile work” show?
answers: It is a special day of sacred assembly and abstaining from work
It is an ordinary workday
It is a day devoted only to counting
questions.explanation: The verse joins sacred assembly with a prohibition against servile work.

questions.question: Why are the loaves called “firstfruits”?
answers: They are eaten first at every meal
They are the first produce dedicated to the Lord
They are baked only at the beginning of the year
questions.explanation: “Firstfruits” means the first produce brought and dedicated to the Lord.

questions.question: How many animals are mentioned in all the offerings in verses 18–19?
answers: Ten
Eleven
Thirteen
questions.explanation: There are seven lambs, one bull, two rams, one goat, and two lambs—thirteen animals in all.

paragraphs.title: Gifts for the Poor from the Harvest

easy.question: For whom must the edges of the field and the gleanings be left?
answers: The poor and the stranger
The king and the priests
Children only
easy.explanation: The passage says to leave them for the poor and the stranger.

easy.question: What must not be done during the harvest?
answers: Watering the field
Clearing the field completely
Selling the grain
easy.explanation: The edges must not be harvested completely, and the gleanings must not be gathered.

easy.question: What are “gleanings”?
answers: The first fruit in the field
The plot beside the house
Grain that falls during the harvest
easy.explanation: Gleanings are the stalks left behind or dropped during harvesting.

medium.question: What should the landowner do after leaving the edges and gleanings?
answers: Leave them for the poor and the stranger
Burn them
Keep them for himself
medium.explanation: They are to remain available for the poor and the stranger.

medium.question: What does “make clean riddance” mean in “thou shalt not make clean riddance of the corners”?
answers: Do not clear or harvest everything
Do not water the field
Do not plant again
medium.explanation: The command means not to harvest the field completely.

medium.question: Why must all the harvest not be gathered?
answers: So the field can rest
So the poor and stranger have something to gather
So harvesting lasts longer
medium.explanation: The purpose is to provide food for the poor and the stranger.

challenge.question: What is the difference between the corners of the field and the gleanings?
answers: The corners are the edges left unharvested; gleanings are what falls during harvest
The corners are grain that was sold; gleanings are seed
There is no difference
challenge.explanation: The verse identifies two different sources of food for the poor: the field’s edges and fallen grain.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from mentioning both the poor and the stranger?
answers: Only landowners may gather
The command serves different groups in need
The stranger must give the harvest to the poor
challenge.explanation: The command extends access to the harvest to both the poor and resident foreigners.

challenge.question: What is emphasized by “I am the Lord your God”?
answers: This is only an agricultural custom
The harvest belongs only to priests
Care for the poor and stranger is the Lord’s command
challenge.explanation: The closing statement shows that leaving the harvest is a divine obligation, not merely a personal choice.

questions.question: What is the difference between the corners of the field and the gleanings?
answers: The corners are the edges left unharvested; gleanings are what falls during harvest
The corners are grain that was sold; gleanings are seed
There is no difference
questions.explanation: The verse identifies two different sources of food for the poor: the field’s edges and fallen grain.

questions.question: What can be inferred from mentioning both the poor and the stranger?
answers: Only landowners may gather
The command serves different groups in need
The stranger must give the harvest to the poor
questions.explanation: The command extends access to the harvest to both the poor and resident foreigners.

questions.question: What is emphasized by “I am the Lord your God”?
answers: This is only an agricultural custom
The harvest belongs only to priests
Care for the poor and stranger is the Lord’s command
questions.explanation: The closing statement shows that leaving the harvest is a divine obligation, not merely a personal choice.

easy.question: In which month does the day described here occur?
answers: The seventh month
The first month
The third month
easy.explanation: The passage says it occurs in the seventh month.

easy.question: On which day of the month does the feast occur?
answers: The tenth day
The first day
The seventh day
easy.explanation: It occurs on the first day of the month.

easy.question: What is forbidden on this day?
answers: Eating meat
Leaving the house
Doing servile work
easy.explanation: The passage forbids servile work.

medium.question: Which description matches this day?
answers: A Sabbath, a memorial of blowing of trumpets, and a holy convocation
A day of fasting, travel, and war
A workday, celebration, and market day
medium.explanation: The verse calls it a Sabbath, a memorial of blowing of trumpets, and a holy convocation.

medium.question: What does “a sabbath” mean in this context?
answers: A day of rest and stopping work
A day of battle
A day of gathering crops
medium.explanation: The following command not to do servile work shows that it is a day of rest.

medium.question: What are the people commanded to do after the prohibition of work?
answers: Build a new altar
Offer an offering made by fire to the Lord
Leave the camp
medium.explanation: The verse commands an offering made by fire to the Lord.

challenge.question: What is the correct order of the details in the passage?
answers: The day is appointed, its holy character is described, work is forbidden, and an offering is mentioned
An offering is made, work is done, and then the day is appointed
The people go to war, fast, and then hold a holy convocation
challenge.explanation: The passage first establishes the date, describes the day, forbids work, and mentions the offering.

challenge.question: Who is commanded to communicate these instructions to Israel?
answers: The priests
Moses
The elders
challenge.explanation: The Lord speaks to Moses and tells him to speak to the children of Israel.

challenge.question: What distinguishes this day from an ordinary day of rest?
answers: It falls on the first day of the seventh month and includes trumpet blasts and an offering
It occurs every day of the week
It is intended only for the nation’s leaders
challenge.explanation: The passage gives it a specific date and adds trumpet remembrance, holy assembly, and an offering.

questions.question: What is the correct order of the details in the passage?
answers: The day is appointed, its holy character is described, work is forbidden, and an offering is mentioned
An offering is made, work is done, and then the day is appointed
The people go to war, fast, and then hold a holy convocation
questions.explanation: The passage first establishes the date, describes the day, forbids work, and mentions the offering.

questions.question: Who is commanded to communicate these instructions to Israel?
answers: The priests
Moses
The elders
questions.explanation: The Lord speaks to Moses and tells him to speak to the children of Israel.

questions.question: What distinguishes this day from an ordinary day of rest?
answers: It falls on the first day of the seventh month and includes trumpet blasts and an offering
It occurs every day of the week
It is intended only for the nation’s leaders
questions.explanation: The passage gives it a specific date and adds trumpet remembrance, holy assembly, and an offering.

paragraphs.title: The Day of Atonement and Self-Denial

easy.question: On what day of the month does the Day of Atonement occur?
answers: The tenth day of the seventh month
The first day of the first month
The fifteenth day of the eighth month
easy.explanation: It occurs on the tenth day of the seventh month.

easy.question: What is this day called?
answers: The Day of Trumpet Blasts
The Day of Atonement
The Feast of Booths
easy.explanation: The passage calls it the Day of Atonement.

easy.question: What is forbidden on this day?
answers: Eating fruit
Studying the Torah
Doing any work
easy.explanation: The passage says, “Ye shall do no work in that same day.”

medium.question: What is the relationship between the work restriction and the purpose of the day?
answers: The day is for making atonement before the Lord
Work would make the feast begin late
Work is forbidden only to save property
medium.explanation: The passage explains that the day is for atonement before the Lord.

medium.question: In “ye shall afflict your souls,” what does “afflict” mean here?
answers: Rejoice greatly
Humble or deny yourselves, including by fasting
Go on a journey
medium.explanation: The context refers to self-denial and traditionally includes fasting.

medium.question: What happens to someone who does not observe the command to afflict himself?
answers: He becomes a priest
He must work more
He is cut off from his people
medium.explanation: The passage says that such a person will be cut off from his people.

challenge.question: Why is “in that same day” repeated in the passage?
answers: To emphasize that the commands apply on that very day
To show that the day is unusually short
To announce that the feast lasts a month
challenge.explanation: The repetition emphasizes that the restrictions apply specifically on the Day of Atonement.

challenge.question: What difference is presented between failing to afflict oneself and doing work?
answers: Only the person who works is punished
A serious punishment is described for each offense
The person who does not afflict himself receives a reward
challenge.explanation: The passage describes a separate severe consequence for each failure.

challenge.question: What follows from combining “holy convocation” with the work prohibition?
answers: It is an ordinary day with a festive name
Only priests must observe it
It is a special day for the whole community requiring special conduct
challenge.explanation: The day is a public holy assembly and no work is permitted.

questions.question: Why is “in that same day” repeated in the passage?
answers: To emphasize that the commands apply on that very day
To show that the day is unusually short
To announce that the feast lasts a month
questions.explanation: The repetition emphasizes that the restrictions apply specifically on the Day of Atonement.

questions.question: What difference is presented between failing to afflict oneself and doing work?
answers: Only the person who works is punished
A serious punishment is described for each offense
The person who does not afflict himself receives a reward
questions.explanation: The passage describes a separate severe consequence for each failure.

questions.question: What follows from combining “holy convocation” with the work prohibition?
answers: It is an ordinary day with a festive name
Only priests must observe it
It is a special day for the whole community requiring special conduct
questions.explanation: The day is a public holy assembly and no work is permitted.

paragraphs.title: Rest and Self-Denial on the Day of Atonement

easy.question: What is forbidden according to these verses?
answers: All work
Only fieldwork
Only household work
easy.explanation: The passage says, “Ye shall do no manner of work.”

easy.question: From what time to what time does the rest last?
answers: Morning to night
Evening to evening
Noon to morning
easy.explanation: The passage says, “from even unto even.”

easy.question: What are the people commanded to do with regard to themselves?
answers: Rejoice
Eat a large meal
Afflict themselves
easy.explanation: The passage commands, “ye shall afflict your souls.”

medium.question: Why is the day called “a sabbath of rest”?
answers: Because it is a day of complete rest
Because it always falls on Saturday
Because only fieldwork is forbidden
medium.explanation: The phrase emphasizes special rest together with the prohibition of all work.

medium.question: What does “afflict your souls” mean in this context?
answers: Make yourselves happy
Humble or deny yourselves, such as by abstaining from food
Tell your souls a story
medium.explanation: The context indicates self-denial; traditionally this includes fasting.

medium.question: When does the observance begin?
answers: The morning of the ninth day
Noon on the ninth day
The evening of the ninth day
medium.explanation: The passage says it begins on the evening of the ninth day and continues from evening to evening.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from “a statute for ever throughout your generations, in all your dwellings”?
answers: The command applies to every generation and every place where they live
It applied only to the wilderness generation
It applies only in one location
challenge.explanation: The wording extends the command through all generations and all dwelling places.

challenge.question: What is the difference between “in the ninth day of the month, at even” and “from even unto even”?
answers: The first marks the end of the day and the second its beginning
The first gives the starting point, and the second gives the duration
They have exactly the same meaning
challenge.explanation: The first identifies when the observance begins; the second explains how long it lasts.

challenge.question: Which combination of commands appears in these verses?
answers: Work a little and rejoice greatly
Fast without stopping work
Stop working and afflict yourselves
challenge.explanation: The verses combine a prohibition of work with the command to afflict oneself.

questions.question: What can be inferred from “a statute for ever throughout your generations, in all your dwellings”?
answers: The command applies to every generation and every place where they live
It applied only to the wilderness generation
It applies only in one location
questions.explanation: The wording extends the command through all generations and all dwelling places.

questions.question: What is the difference between “in the ninth day of the month, at even” and “from even unto even”?
answers: The first marks the end of the day and the second its beginning
The first gives the starting point, and the second gives the duration
They have exactly the same meaning
questions.explanation: The first identifies when the observance begins; the second explains how long it lasts.

questions.question: Which combination of commands appears in these verses?
answers: Work a little and rejoice greatly
Fast without stopping work
Stop working and afflict yourselves
questions.explanation: The verses combine a prohibition of work with the command to afflict oneself.

paragraphs.title: The Feast of Booths and Its Offerings

easy.question: How long does the Feast of Booths last?
answers: Seven days
Eight days
Three days
easy.explanation: The passage calls it a seven-day feast.

easy.question: What is forbidden on the first day of the feast?
answers: Eating in a booth
Doing servile work
Offering a sacrifice
easy.explanation: No servile work is to be done on the first day.

easy.question: On which day is there an additional holy convocation after the seven feast days?
answers: The second day
The seventh day
The eighth day
easy.explanation: The eighth day is also a holy convocation.

medium.question: What are the Israelites commanded to do during the seven days?
answers: Offer offerings made by fire to the Lord
Stop all prayer
Fast every day
medium.explanation: The passage commands offerings made by fire throughout the seven days.

medium.question: What does “solemn assembly” mean in this context?
answers: A large meal
A day of cessation and assembly
The beginning of the harvest
medium.explanation: The eighth day is a special closing assembly on which work is forbidden.

medium.question: What is the relationship between the seven feast days and the eighth day?
answers: The eighth day replaces all seven days
The eighth day is the first day of the feast
A further holy day follows the seven feast days
medium.explanation: The passage describes seven days and then an additional holy eighth day.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from mentioning both the seven feast days and the eighth day?
answers: The eighth day is separate and has a special holy status
The feast lasts only one day
No offering is required on the eighth day
challenge.explanation: The eighth day is separately described as a holy convocation with an offering and no servile work.

challenge.question: What does “every thing upon his day” mean regarding the offerings?
answers: All offerings are made only at the end
The required offerings are made on each appointed day
Offerings are made only when someone makes a vow
challenge.explanation: The phrase indicates that each day has its own required offerings.

challenge.question: What is emphasized about gifts, vows, and freewill offerings?
answers: They cancel the feast offerings
They are permitted only on the first day
They are in addition to the feast offerings and the Lord’s Sabbaths
challenge.explanation: The repeated “beside” shows that these gifts are additional, not substitutes.

questions.question: What can be inferred from mentioning both the seven feast days and the eighth day?
answers: The eighth day is separate and has a special holy status
The feast lasts only one day
No offering is required on the eighth day
questions.explanation: The eighth day is separately described as a holy convocation with an offering and no servile work.

questions.question: What does “every thing upon his day” mean regarding the offerings?
answers: All offerings are made only at the end
The required offerings are made on each appointed day
Offerings are made only when someone makes a vow
questions.explanation: The phrase indicates that each day has its own required offerings.

questions.question: What is emphasized about gifts, vows, and freewill offerings?
answers: They cancel the feast offerings
They are permitted only on the first day
They are in addition to the feast offerings and the Lord’s Sabbaths
questions.explanation: The repeated “beside” shows that these gifts are additional, not substitutes.

paragraphs.title: Rejoicing at the Feast of Booths and the Four Species

easy.question: On what date does the feast begin?
answers: The fifteenth day of the seventh month
The first day of the first month
The twentieth day of the eighth month
easy.explanation: The feast begins on the fifteenth day of the seventh month.

easy.question: How long does the feast last?
answers: One day
Seven days
Eight days
easy.explanation: The passage says to celebrate the feast for seven days.

easy.question: What are the people commanded to take on the first day?
answers: Bread, wine, and oil
Clothing, water, and tools
Fruit of a goodly tree, palm branches, leafy branches, and willows
easy.explanation: The passage lists these four kinds of branches and fruit.

medium.question: What is the connection between gathering the produce of the land and the feast?

The produce is gathered only after the feast

A day of rest and cessation from work
A day for gathering produce

paragraphs.title: The Perpetual Statute of the Feast of Booths

easy.question: How long does the Feast of Booths last?
answers: Seven days
Three days
Fourteen days
easy.explanation: The passage says the feast lasts seven days.

easy.question: Where are the Israelites commanded to dwell during the feast?
answers: In houses
In booths
In the Temple
easy.explanation: The passage says, “Ye shall dwell in booths seven days.”

easy.question: What are the Israelites to remember by dwelling in booths?
answers: The building of Jerusalem
The giving of the Torah
That the Lord made Israel dwell in booths when he brought them from Egypt
easy.explanation: The booths recall Israel’s experience during the exodus from Egypt.

medium.question: Why are the Israelites commanded to dwell in booths?
answers: So future generations will know about the exodus
To prepare for war
To mark the beginning of the year
medium.explanation: The passage says the purpose is for future generations to know what happened.

medium.question: What can be understood from “all that are Israelites born shall dwell in booths”?
answers: Only priests must dwell in booths
The command applies to all native Israelites
Only those who left Egypt must dwell in booths
medium.explanation: The wording applies the command to all native Israelites.

medium.question: What does “statute” mean in “a statute for ever throughout your generations”?
answers: A story from the past
A dwelling place
A permanent command for future generations
medium.explanation: Here it means an enduring law or command to be observed by succeeding generations.

challenge.question: If someone from a later generation asks why people dwell in booths, what answer best fits the passage?
answers: To remember that the Lord made Israel dwell in booths during the exodus
To remember the names of Israel’s kings
To mark the beginning of the rainy season
challenge.explanation: The passage explicitly gives Israel’s wilderness experience as the reason.

challenge.question: What does “a statute for ever throughout your generations” teach about the Feast of Booths?
answers: It was observed only in the wilderness
The command is to continue from generation to generation
The feast occurs only once
challenge.explanation: The wording emphasizes the lasting and generational nature of the command.

challenge.question: What is the function of “that” in “That your generations may know”?
answers: It gives the date of the feast
It gives the place of dwelling
It introduces the purpose of dwelling in booths
challenge.explanation: The phrase explains the purpose: future generations are to know the exodus tradition.

answers: Moses
Aaron
Joshua

easy.question: To whom did Moses speak?
answers: The priests only
The children of Israel
The kings of the nations

easy.question: What did Moses speak about?
answers: Building the Tabernacle
The exodus from Egypt
The feasts of the Lord

medium.question: What was Moses’ purpose in speaking to the Israelites?
answers: To communicate the Lord’s appointed feasts
To appoint a king
To describe the wilderness journeys
medium.explanation: Moses conveyed the instructions concerning the Lord’s feasts.

medium.question: What does “feasts” mean in “the feasts of the Lord”?
answers: Places to live
Appointed times of the Lord
Holy vessels
medium.explanation: Here “feasts” refers to appointed sacred times or festivals.

medium.question: What can be understood from this verse appearing after the list of feasts?
answers: The feasts were canceled
The feasts were intended only for Moses
The instructions were delivered to the Israelites
medium.explanation: The verse summarizes that Moses communicated the whole matter to Israel.

challenge.question: What does “the feasts of the Lord” show about their authority?
answers: They belong to the Lord and are established by him
They were established by Israel’s kings
They were Moses’ private customs
challenge.explanation: The title attributes the feasts to the Lord rather than to an individual.

challenge.question: Who is the message addressed to, according to “the children of Israel”?
answers: Moses alone
The whole people of Israel
The high priest alone
challenge.explanation: The phrase identifies the entire Israelite community as the audience.

challenge.question: What role of Moses is reflected in the verse?
answers: Inventor of the feasts
King who decides the feasts
Messenger who conveys the Lord’s instructions to the people
challenge.explanation: Moses is presented as the one who declares the Lord’s feasts to Israel.
